data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The preference for better-corroborated theories is defensible on Popper's terms as a pragmatic, non-inductive rule of action akin to betting on the horse with the best track record without believing it will win next time.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the choice implies an expectation of future success based on past performance, it surrenders to induction.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If 'acting on' a theory requires believing it is approximately true or reliable, the distinction collapses.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Corroboration functions as a selection filter for 'fitness' in an evolutionary epistemology; choosing the fittest theory is a survival strategy, not a probability assignment. The mechanism is 'conjecture and refutation' acting as a sieve, where the remaining theory is simply the last one standing, not the most likely true one.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
